exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext DNS queries can be intercepted via network sniffing since they are transmitted unencrypted.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS is the protocol used in plaintext query interception, making this technique directly relevant.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Compromising or spoofing DNS server responses is the core mechanism of DNS response spoofing without DNSSEC.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can acquire DNS server infrastructure to conduct spoofing attacks when DNSSEC is absent.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of DoT enforcement allows attackers to exploit unencrypted DNS channels for covert communication or tunneling.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Calculation
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS Calculation involves manipulating DNS responses, directly relevant to birthday attack-based cache poisoning.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS/Passive DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Zone transfers expose DNS records which attackers can collect through passive DNS reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted zone transfers leak DNS information that adversaries can gather for target reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Replaying or exploiting weak TSIG MACs enables adversary-in-the-middle attacks on DNS zone update transactions.
